A long page for cap testing

Paragraph 1. Reading in a second language is a skill that improves with deliberate practice.

Paragraph 2. A good translation preserves meaning, tone and the rhythm of the original sentence.

Paragraph 3. Interfaces should disappear while you read and return only when you need them.

Paragraph 4. Caching turns a slow network into an instant reading experience on repeat visits.

Paragraph 5. Chunking text into paragraphs keeps context intact and avoids sentence fragments.

Paragraph 6. Latency is a feature: the first visible paragraph matters more than the last.

Paragraph 7. Error states should always tell the reader what to do next.

Paragraph 8. A glossary protects product names and technical terms from being rewritten.

Paragraph 9. Dark pages need their own palette, not a global light theme.

Paragraph 10. Users notice layout shifts more than they notice animation.

Paragraph 11. Open source means the privacy claims can be verified, not just trusted.

Paragraph 12. The best reading tool is the one you forget you are using.
